plan.hypothesis: Omnibus null hypothesis: all three group means are equal. Alternative: at least one group mean differs.

Three independent groups with normal distributions
Common variance (homogeneity of variance)
Fixed effects model
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 reflects the effect size
Omnibus F test with k=3 groups
scientific_notes: Eta-squared converts to noncentrality parameter λ via the relationship with f (Cohen's effect size): f² = η² / (1 - η²), so f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) where N is total sample size
The F distribution has numerator df = k - 1 = 2 and denominator df = N - k = 3n - 3
Inversion will find the minimum integer n per group satisfying power ≥ 0.80
Report achieved power at the selected design and the preceding admissible design

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.06, the minimum sample size per group required to achieve 80% power at alpha = 0.05 for the omnibus F test is 52 participants per group (156 total participants). The continuous solution was 51.33 participants per group. At n=52, achieved power is 80.56%; at the preceding design (n=51), power is 79.73%, confirming that n=52 is the minimum integer meeting the power requirement.
answer.method: One-way ANOVA sample size inversion using pwr.anova.test() (R package pwr v1.3-0). Eta-squared (η² = 0.06) was converted to Cohen's f via f = √(η²/(1-η²)) = 0.2526. The function inverts the non-central F distribution with numerator df = k-1 = 2 and denominator df = N-k = 3n-3 to find n satisfying the power equation. The continuous solution was rounded up to the nearest integer and verified at both selected and preceding integer designs.

# One-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Design: 3 groups, balanced, common variance
# Population eta-squared = 0.06
# Target power = 0.80, alpha = 0.05

# Install/load required package for power analysis
if (!require("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pwr", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  library("pwr")
}

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3  # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# f = sqrt(f²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("Effect size conversion:\n")
cat("  eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  f²:", f_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f, "\n\n")

# Use pwr.anova.test() to find the minimum n per group
# This function uses the non-centrality parameter approach
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,          # number of groups
  f = f,          # effect size (Cohen's f)
  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)

n_per_group_continuous <- result$n
power_at_continuous <- result$power

cat("Continuous solution from pwr.anova.test():\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group_continuous, "\n")
cat("  power:", power_at_continuous, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer to ensure power ≥ target
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("Rounded integer solution:\n")
cat("  n per group:", n_per_group, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the selected design (n = ceiling result)
result_selected <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  n = n_per_group,
  f = f,
  sig.level = alpha
)

power_selected <- result_selected$power

cat("Power at selected design (n =", n_per_group, "):\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the preceding design (n - 1)
n_preceding <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_preceding >= 2) {  # minimum sensible sample size
  result_preceding <- pwr.anova.test(
    k = k,
    n = n_preceding,
    f = f,
    sig.level = alpha
  )
  power_preceding <- result_preceding$power
  
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
  cat("  Power:", power_preceding, "\n\n")
} else {
  power_preceding <- NA
  cat("Preceding design not available (would be n < 2)\n\n")
}

# Summary
cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", k * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (numerator):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (denominator):", k * n_per_group - k, "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = n_per_group,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_sample_size",
      value = k * n_per_group,
      unit = "participants"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design",
      value = round(power_selected, 4),
      unit = "probability"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design",
      value = if(!is.na(power_preceding)) round(power_preceding, 4) else NA,
      unit = "probability"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "cohens_f",
      value = round(f, 4),
      unit = "unitless"
    )
  )
)

cat("\nJSON output:\n")
print(jsonlite::toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent verification of one-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Using direct non-centrality parameter and F-distribution approach

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3                    # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# η² = f² × (k - 1) / (1 + f² × (k - 1)) is one relationship
# But the standard formula is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("=== EFFECT SIZE CONVERSION ===\n")
cat("η² = ", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("f² = η² / (1 - η²) = ", eta_squared, " / ", 1 - eta_squared, " = ", f_squared, "\n")
cat("f = sqrt(f²) = ", f, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Verify the relationship between η² and f in ANOVA context
# For ANOVA, η² = SS_between / SS_total
# Cohen's f is defined as f = sqrt(SS_between / SS_within)
# The relationship is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# This is correctly applied in the candidate answer.

# Step 3: Test using base R and non-central F distribution
# For a given n per group:
# - Total sample size N = k × n
# - Numerator df: df1 = k - 1 = 2
# - Denominator df: df2 = N - k = k(n - 1) = 3n - 3
# - Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) = f × sqrt(k × n)

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n per group
compute_power_anova <- function(n_per_group, k, f, alpha) {
  N <- k * n_per_group
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- N - k
  lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
  
  # Critical F value for the given alpha
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true)
  # Under H1, F follows non-central F distribution with noncentrality λ
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(power = power, lambda = lambda, df1 = df1, df2 = df2))
}

# Test at n = 52
result_52 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 52, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 52 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 52, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*52, ") = ", result_52$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_52$df1, ", df2 = ", result_52$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 51
result_51 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 51, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 51 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 51, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*51, ") = ", result_51$lambda, "\n")
cat("df1 = ", result_51$df1, ", df2 = ", result_51$df2, "\n")
cat("Power at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n\n")

# Test at n = 50
result_50 <- compute_power_anova(n_per_group = 50, k = k, f = f, alpha = alpha)
cat("=== POWER AT n = 50 ===\n")
cat("Total N = ", 3 * 50, "\n")
cat("Power at n=50: ", result_50$power, "\n\n")

# Verify: n=52 should give power ≥ 0.80, and n=51 should give power < 0.80
cat("=== VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Does n=52 achieve target power 0.80? ", result_52$power >= 0.80, "\n")
cat("Does n=51 fall short of target power 0.80? ", result_51$power < 0.80, "\n")

# Compare with candidate answer
cat("\n=== COMPARISON WITH CANDIDATE ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Candidate reported power at n=52: 0.8055643919819825\n")
cat("Independent computation at n=52: ", result_52$power, "\n")
cat("Difference: ", abs(result_52$power - 0.8055643919819825), "\n\n")

cat("Candidate reported power at n=51: 0.7972572678090943\n")
cat("Independent computation at n=51: ", result_51$power, "\n")
cat("Difference: ", abs(result_51$power - 0.7972572678090943), "\n\n")

# Final result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n52", value = result_52$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n51", value = result_51$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "independent_power_at_n50", value = result_50$power, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "minimum_n_confirmed", value = 52, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "match_with_candidate", value = abs(result_52$power - 0.8055643919819825) < 0.00001, unit = "boolean")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat(POWER_AGENT_RESULT)

  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)

# Independent verification of one-way ANOVA sample size calculation
# Using direct non-centrality parameter and F-distribution approach

# Parameters
eta_squared <- 0.06
k <- 3                    # number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f
# η² = f² × (k - 1) / (1 + f² × (k - 1)) is one relationship
# But the standard formula is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
f_squared <- eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared)
f <- sqrt(f_squared)

cat("=== EFFECT SIZE CONVERSION ===\n")
cat("η² = ", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("f² = η² / (1 - η²) = ", eta_squared, " / ", 1 - eta_squared, " = ", f_squared, "\n")
cat("f = sqrt(f²) = ", f, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Verify the relationship between η² and f in ANOVA context
# For ANOVA, η² = SS_between / SS_total
# Cohen's f is defined as f = sqrt(SS_between / SS_within)
# The relationship is: f² = η² / (1 - η²)
# This is correctly applied in the candidate answer.

# Step 3: Test using base R and non-central F distribution
# For a given n per group:
# - Total sample size N = k × n
# - Numerator df: df1 = k - 1 = 2
# - Denominator df: df2 = N - k = k(n - 1) = 3n - 3
# - Noncentrality parameter: λ = f × sqrt(N) = f × sqrt(k × n)

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n per group
compute_power_anova <- function(n_per_group, k, f, alpha) {
  N <- k * n_per_group
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- N - k
  lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
  
  # Critical F value for the given alpha
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | H1 true)
  # Under H1, F follows non-central F distribution with noncentrality λ
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(power = power, lambda = lambda, df1 = df1, df2 = df2))
}

cat("Total N = ", 3 * 52, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality λ = f × sqrt(N) = ", f, " × sqrt(", 3*52, ") = ", result_52$lambda, "\n")

cat("  f²:", f_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f, "\n\n")

  k = k,          # number of groups
  f = f,          # effect size (Cohen's f)
  sig.level = alpha,  # significance level
  power = target_power  # target power
)
